# tccquickr

Compiles a declared subset of R to C, Fortran and in-memory TinyCC kernels.

You declare the types of a function's arguments with `declare(type(...))`.
tccquickr infers the type, shape and effects of every value from there, and
either produces a kernel that matches R or tells you why it cannot. It never
falls back to calling R.

## Installation

```r
install.packages(
  "tccquickr",
  repos = c("https://sounkou-bioinfo.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos"))
)
```

## A first kernel

Declarations follow quickr: `double(n, p)` is a double matrix with `n` rows
and `p` columns. Symbols name dimensions, so two arguments that share `p` must
agree on it.

```{r declare}
library(tccquickr)

matrix_vector <- function(x, w) {
  declare(type(x = double(n, p), w = double(p)))
  x %*% w
}
```

Analysis, backend planning and the product are separate steps. These two
helpers return the generated C source and a callable compiled in memory by
TinyCC through Rtinycc:

```{r helpers}
c_source <- function(fn) {
  plan <- tccq_plan_backend(
    tccq_analyze(fn, strict = TRUE)@value,
    tccq_c_backend(),
    tccq_backend_context(mode = "source", target = "c")
  )
  plan@value@products@attrs$source
}

jit <- function(fn, registry = tccq_default_op_registry()) {
  plan <- tccq_plan_backend(
    tccq_analyze(fn, registry = registry, strict = TRUE)@value,
    tccq_rtinycc_backend(),
    tccq_backend_context(mode = "jit", target = "c")
  )
  plan@value@products@attrs$callable
}
```

The product is one loop nest: a map over `n` and a sum over `p`.

```{r generated-c}
cat(c_source(matrix_vector))
```

The compiled function agrees with R:

```{r run-jit}
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(12), nrow = 3)
w <- rnorm(4)
all.equal(jit(matrix_vector)(x, w), drop(x %*% w))
```

The boundary checks the shared dimension `p`:

```{r boundary-check}
try(jit(matrix_vector)(x, rnorm(5)))
```

## Shapes are facts

Slice bounds such as `n - 2L` become dimensions of the result, so a stencil
reads shifted elements in one loop and builds no slice copies. Dimension
symbols exist only for the compiler: in plain R, `n` is unbound, so the
comparison spells out the extents.

```{r stencil}
stencil <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  x[1:(n - 2L)] + x[2:(n - 1L)] + x[3:n]
}
v <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64)
identical(jit(stencil)(v), v[1:5] + v[2:6] + v[3:7])
```

## Fusion

A local used once, by the next statement, is computed in the loop that
reads it. `scaled` below gets no buffer, and the kernel has one loop:

```{r fusion}
affine <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  scaled <- x * 2
  scaled + 1
}
cat(c_source(affine))
```

Fusion must not change which warnings R raises, or their order. `sqrt()` can
warn, so a `sqrt()` local gets its own buffer and loop, and is computed in
full before it is used:

```{r fusion-refused}
root_then_exp <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  root <- sqrt(x)
  exp(root)
}
cat(c_source(root_then_exp))
```

Double arithmetic follows IEEE 754 and cannot warn, so the fused kernel is
bit-identical to R on missing and infinite values:

```{r fusion-special-values}
specials <- c(1.5, NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf, 0, 1e308)
identical(jit(affine)(specials), affine(specials))
```

## Several loop nests

A reduction that later work depends on becomes its own nest, and its result
is stored in a scalar that the next nest reads.

```{r multi-nest}
normalize <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  s <- sum(x)
  x / s
}
cat(c_source(normalize))
v <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
all.equal(jit(normalize)(v), v / sum(v))
```

## Loops, indexing and branches

`for` over `seq_len()` of a declared extent compiles to a C loop. An index
such as `x[index]` is accepted only when the compiler can prove it is in
bounds.

```{r loops}
indexed_sum <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  total <- 0
  for (index in seq_len(n)) total <- total + x[index]
  total
}
identical(jit(indexed_sum)(c(1, 2, 3)), 6)

matrix_sum <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n, p)))
  total <- 0
  for (row in seq_len(n)) {
    for (column in seq_len(p)) total <- total + x[row, column]
  }
  total
}
m <- matrix(1:6 + 0, nrow = 2)
identical(jit(matrix_sum)(m), sum(m))
```

An index the compiler cannot prove in bounds is refused. The result names
the unproven fact:

```{r unproven-index}
shifted_sum <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  total <- 0
  for (index in seq_len(n)) total <- total + x[index + 1L]
  total
}
refused <- tccq_analyze(shifted_sum)
refused@diagnostics[[1L]]@code
refused@diagnostics[[1L]]@verdict
```

An `if` with a scalar logical condition evaluates only the selected arm, as
R does:

```{r branch}
guarded_sum <- function(x, flag) {
  declare(type(x = double(n), flag = logical()))
  if (flag) sum(x) else 0
}
c(jit(guarded_sum)(c(1, 2), TRUE), jit(guarded_sum)(c(1, 2), FALSE))
```

## New operations

An operation can be defined by an R expression over its parameters. The
compiler expands it inline and checks that the expansion stays within the
declared effect, so `sigmoid()` fuses like any built-in:

```{r new-operation}
sigmoid_registry <- tccq_op_registry_add(
  tccq_default_op_registry(),
  tccq_op_impl(
    "sigmoid",
    target = "neutral",
    region_kind = "kernel",
    effect = tccq_effect(reads = TRUE, may_warn = TRUE),
    body = tccq_op_body(function(value) 1 / (1 + exp(-value))),
    elementwise = tccq_elementwise_spec(
      "sigmoid",
      1L,
      result_type = function(input_types, result_shape) {
        tccq_type("double", result_shape)
      }
    )
  )
)

logistic <- function(x) {
  declare(type(x = double(n)))
  sigmoid(x)
}
v <- c(-2, 0, 2)
all.equal(jit(logistic, sigmoid_registry)(v), 1 / (1 + exp(-v)))
```

## A type checker for R

`tccq_analyze()` needs no backend, so it also works as a checker. Each
diagnostic carries a verdict:

- `refuted`: R fails as well.
- `unproven`: R might succeed, but the declarations do not prove what the
  compiler needs. `data$requires` names the missing fact.
- `unsupported`: valid R outside the compiled subset.

```{r verdicts}
check <- function(fn) {
  result <- tccq_analyze(fn)
  if (result@success) {
    return(data.frame(code = "ok", verdict = "", requires = ""))
  }
  d <- result@diagnostics[[1L]]
  data.frame(
    code = d@code,
    verdict = d@verdict,
    requires = paste(d@data$requires, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

programs <- list(
  conformable = function(x, w) {
    declare(type(x = double(n, p), w = double(p)))
    x %*% w
  },
  fixed_mismatch = function(x, w) {
    declare(type(x = double(3, 4), w = double(5)))
    x %*% w
  },
  symbolic_mismatch = function(x, w) {
    declare(type(x = double(n, p), w = double(q)))
    x %*% w
  },
  transposed = function(x, y) {
    declare(type(x = double(n, p), y = double(p, n)))
    x + y
  },
  outside_subset = function(x) {
    declare(type(x = double(n)))
    paste(x)
  }
)
knitr::kable(cbind(program = names(programs), do.call(rbind, lapply(programs, check))),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

The checker types more of R than the backends emit. `log()` can warn
"NaNs produced", which no kernel reports yet, so it is typed and has no
generated code:

```{r typed-only}
log_ratio <- function(x, y) {
  declare(type(x = double(n, p), y = double(n, p)))
  log(x) - log(y)
}
analysis <- tccq_analyze(log_ratio)
analysis@success
result <- analysis@value@values[[analysis@value@result]]
c(base = result@type@base, rank = result@type@shape@rank)

compiled <- tccq_compile(log_ratio, strict = FALSE)
compiled@diagnostics[[1L]]@code
compiled@diagnostics[[1L]]@verdict
```

## Where the subset ends

These programs are the current targets. Each one either compiles or stops
at a named diagnostic. The table is computed when this file is knit.

```{r targets}
targets <- list(
  logistic_gradient = function(x, y, w, lambda) {
    declare(type(x = double(n, p), y = double(n), w = double(p), lambda = double()))
    mu <- colMeans(x)
    sigma <- sqrt(colSums((x - mu)^2) / (n - 1L))
    z <- (x - mu) / sigma
    prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(z %*% w)))
    w - 0.01 * (crossprod(z, prob - y) / n + lambda * w)
  },
  raw_roundtrip = function(x) {
    declare(type(x = raw(n)))
    x
  },
  repeat_switch = function(x, flag) {
    declare(type(x = double(n), flag = logical()))
    out <- 0
    i <- 1L
    repeat {
      if (i > n) break
      out <- out + ifelse(flag, x[i], -x[i])
      i <- i + 1L
    }
    switch(if (flag) "sum" else "neg", sum = out, neg = -out)
  },
  apply_reduce = function(x) {
    declare(type(x = double(n, p)))
    Reduce(`+`, lapply(seq_len(p), function(j) sum(x[, j])))
  }
)
status <- function(fn) {
  compiled <- tccq_compile(fn, strict = FALSE)
  if (compiled@success) {
    return(data.frame(status = "compiles", verdict = ""))
  }
  d <- compiled@diagnostics[[1L]]
  data.frame(status = d@code, verdict = d@verdict)
}
knitr::kable(cbind(program = names(targets), do.call(rbind, lapply(targets, status))),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Design

All compiler stages exchange S7 values: types with symbolic shapes,
effects, loop nests, storage plans and backend plans. C, TinyCC and Fortran
render the same backend-neutral loop nests.
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) describes each stage, and
[docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md) lists what comes next.
